items.stem: A function returns a large object that is immediately used and discarded. Which modern C++ feature most directly avoids an unnecessary deep copy?

options.rationale: Correct: move semantics transfer ownership of the resource instead of copying it.
Returning a raw pointer reintroduces manual ownership and leak risk.
inline affects linkage/expansion, not copy avoidance for the returned object.
const on a parameter does not affect how the return value is moved or copied.

items.explanation: Correct: move semantics transfer ownership of the resource instead of copying it.

items.stem: Which smart pointer expresses sole ownership of a heap object with no reference counting overhead?

options.rationale: Correct: unique_ptr models exclusive ownership and has no reference-count overhead.
shared_ptr carries an atomic reference count for shared ownership.
weak_ptr is a non-owning observer of a shared_ptr.
A raw pointer expresses no ownership policy at all.

items.explanation: Correct: unique_ptr models exclusive ownership and has no reference-count overhead.

items.stem: Which TWO are direct benefits of the RAII idiom in C++? (Select TWO)

options.text: Resources are released when their owning object goes out of scope
options.rationale: Correct: the destructor runs deterministically at scope exit, freeing the resource.

options.text: Cleanup still happens when an exception unwinds the stack
options.rationale: Correct: stack unwinding runs destructors, so RAII releases resources on exceptions.

options.text: It removes the need for a type system
options.rationale: RAII is unrelated to whether the language is typed.

options.text: It makes all code run faster
options.rationale: RAII is about correctness of resource release, not raw speed.

items.explanation: Correct: the destructor runs deterministically at scope exit, freeing the resource.
